title: Passive Voice Quiz 3
description: Use modal + be, modal + have been, to be and being in the passive.
instructions: Passive Voice: Modal verbs in the passive.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'You must lock the door'?
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. Watch out: be stays in the base form after must.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'They should have finished the work'?
options: The work should have been finished.
The work should be finished have.
The work should has been finished.
The work should have being finished.
questions.explanation: Past modal passive: modal + have + been + past participle. Watch out: have stays in the base form after should.

questions.question: Tickets can {{1}} {{2}} (buy) online.
questions.explanation: After can the passive uses be and a past participle. Watch out: the participle of buy is bought.

questions.question: The window {{1}} (must / break) by someone during the night. (I am sure.)
questions.explanation: A deduction about the past uses modal + have been + participle: must have been broken. Watch out: be alone would refer to now.

questions.question: 'The report can been finished today' is correct.
questions.explanation: After a modal the verb is be, so the sentence is The report can be finished today. Watch out: been belongs after have, not after a modal.

questions.question: Which sentence is a correct negative passive?
questions.explanation: The negative modal goes in front of be: shouldn't be made. Watch out: don't should is not possible, and the participle is still needed.

questions.question: Choose the missing form after the modal.

rows.given: You can see the stars. The stars can ___ seen.
They might have lost it. It might ___ lost.
We must pay the bill. The bill must ___ paid.
Someone should have told her. She should ___ told.
They will have to sell it. It will have to ___ sold.

questions.explanation: Now needs be, and the past needs have been. Watch out: will have to is followed by be.

questions.question: Match each verb form with its passive pattern.
questions.explanation: Every pattern ends in a past participle. Watch out: being is used after a preposition, and to be after verbs such as want.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The subject, then the modal, then be, then the participle. Watch out: be comes before signed.

questions.question: She left the party without ___ seen.
questions.explanation: After a preposition the -ing form is used: without being seen. Watch out: to be and be are not possible after without.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: The work must have be done.
The letter could have been lost.
questions.explanation: The correct sentences use be after the modal, or have been for the past. Watch out: have be and might been use the wrong form.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: The cake can be ate by everyone.
accepted: The cake can be eaten by everyone.
The cake can be eaten by everyone
questions.explanation: After be the passive needs a past participle: eaten. Watch out: ate is the past simple form.
